title: Treatment instead of jail
intro: A letter asking the prosecutor to let your loved one go to the treatment your family arranged, instead of jail, with full accountability to the prosecutor's office.
privacy: Saved in protected storage on this device for your signed-in account. What you write stays on this phone unless you share it.
before: Give it to their defense attorney first. Most prosecutors expect a request like this to come through the attorney, who may send it, add to it, or time it with a court date. No lawyer yet? Ask for the public defender.
Don't write about what happened or the charges. Anything you put in writing can be used in the case. This letter only talks about treatment and accountability.
The program can send updates to the prosecutor only after your loved one signs a release. Federal privacy rules protect addiction treatment records. Ask the program for its release form.
Choose a licensed program and ask it for an acceptance letter with the admission date. Attach it.
Some courts have drug court or diversion programs with their own rules. The attorney will know which apply.
legalNote: General information, not legal advice. Every county and every case is different.

letter.opening: I am writing as {{name}}'s {{relationship}}. Our family respectfully asks that {{name}} be allowed to enter treatment in place of jail while the charges in this case are pending.
letter.arranged: We have arranged a place for {{name}} at {{program}}. {{name}} can be admitted on {{startDate}}.
letter.askHeading: We ask your office to consider this agreement:
letter.askComplete: {{name}} enters {{program}} on {{startDate}} and completes the full program, including the aftercare plan the program recommends.
letter.askUpdates: {{name}} signs a release so the program can send written progress updates to your office {{updates}}, covering attendance, participation, and progress in treatment.
letter.askEarlyExit: If {{name}} leaves the program before completing it, your office is told right away.
letter.askMeeting: When treatment is complete, your office meets in person with {{name}}'s attorney, and with our family if you are willing, to assess the change in {{name}} and review whether continued prosecution of the pending charges is needed, and, if it is, whether the charges can be reduced.
letter.accountability: We are not asking that this case be set aside. We are asking for the chance for {{name}} to show real change through treatment, with accountability to your office at every step.
letter.attorneyCopy: {{name}}'s attorney, {{attorney}}, has a copy of this letter.
letter.thanks: Thank you for considering this request.
